name: Cape Town Globus Data Path
description: Globus Connect Server endpoints at FIU and/or CIEN whose data traffic to the SANReN Cape Town DTN runs over an L2 facility-port VLAN, while Globus reaches them on public addresses.
description_long: Demonstrates that Globus data can be steered onto a private research path purely by where the endpoints advertise their data interface. Each DTN VM (Rocky 9, one slice per site: FIU, CIEN or both, picked with the Build FIU / Build CIEN checkboxes; FIU only by default) gets a public uplink (AmLight-Layer3-FIU at FIU, FABnetv4Ext at CIEN) on which Globus Connect Server 5.4 is registered, and a data NIC bridged through an L2 facility port (AmLight-EXP-Layer2-FIU at FIU, FP2-CIEN at CIEN) onto the VLAN that reaches the Cape Town DTN; that NIC is GCS's --data-interface. FABRIC offers only VLANs 4000-4094 on AmLight-EXP-Layer2-FIU, so the weave takes a free one and reports it for the operators to map to Cape Town's VLAN 1400 on the switch. The Cape Town side runs Globus Connect Personal, which opens every data connection itself to the advertised address, so the bytes take the VLAN - for transfers submitted from the CLI or the web app alike. The weave checks the address is not already in use, reachability and jumbo frames to Cape Town, the public addresses (no NAT), firewalls the public NIC to 443 + 50000-51000, creates one mapped collection per endpoint, saves each deployment key under results/keys, writes results/legs.json and exits. globus_transfer_demo.ipynb runs transfers to and from the Cape Town collection and proves the path from the DTN's own sockets. Stop deletes each Globus endpoint before its slice, and keeps the slice if that fails.

args.name: SLICE_NAME
args.label: Slice name prefix
args.description: Prefix for the slices: <prefix>-fiu, <prefix>-cien

args.name: BUILD_FIU
args.label: Build FIU DTN
args.description: Build the DTN at FIU (slice <prefix>-fiu): public on AmLight-Layer3-FIU, data on AmLight-EXP-Layer2-FIU.

args.name: BUILD_CIEN
args.label: Build CIEN DTN
args.description: Build the DTN at CIEN too (slice <prefix>-cien). Off while CIEN is offline; the CIEN fields below are used only when this is on.

args.name: FP_BW
args.label: Facility port bandwidth (Gbps)
args.description: Bandwidth reserved on every facility port (above the project limit needs Net.NoLimitBW)

args.name: FIU_PUBLIC
args.label: FIU public uplink
args.description: How Globus reaches the FIU endpoint (443): 'ext' = FABnetv4Ext, or an L3 facility port name

args.name: FIU_PUBLIC_VLAN
args.label: FIU public VLAN
args.description: VLAN AmLight assigned on AmLight-Layer3-FIU

args.name: FIU_PUBLIC_ADDR
args.label: FIU public address
args.description: FIU DTN public IPv4 (CIDR) from AmLight's 67.17.206.72/29; .73 is the gateway

args.name: FIU_PUBLIC_GW
args.label: FIU public gateway
args.description: Blank = first usable address of the subnet (AmLight convention: 67.17.206.73)

args.name: FIU_PUBLIC_ADDR6
args.label: FIU public IPv6
args.description: FIU DTN public IPv6 (CIDR) from AmLight's 2800:bc0:9000:3002::/64; blank = IPv4 only

args.name: FIU_PUBLIC_GW6
args.label: FIU public IPv6 gateway
args.description: Blank = first usable address (2800:bc0:9000:3002::1)

args.name: FIU_L2_IP
args.label: FIU L2 address
args.description: FIU DTN address on the Cape Town VLAN (Cape Town is 10.14.0.50). Refused if another host already answers for it.

args.name: FIU_L2_FP
args.label: FIU L2 facility port
args.description: Facility port for the FIU data path (FABRIC allows VLANs 4000-4094 on it)

args.name: FIU_L2_VLAN
args.label: FIU L2 VLAN
args.description: VLAN on FIU_L2_FP; auto = first free in 4000-4094. The operators map it to Cape Town's VLAN 1400 on the switch - the weave prints which one it took.

args.name: FIU_PEER_IP
args.label: Cape Town IP (FIU VLAN)
args.description: The Cape Town DTN's address on the FIU data VLAN

args.name: FIU_HOST
args.label: FIU host
args.description: Pin the FIU DTN VM to a worker, e.g. fiu-w1.fabric-testbed.net (blank = FABRIC picks)

args.name: CIEN_PUBLIC
args.label: CIEN public uplink (only if Build CIEN)
args.description: How Globus reaches the CIEN endpoint: 'ext' = FABnetv4Ext, or an L3 facility port name (then set CIEN_PUBLIC_ADDR/GW in the environment)

args.name: CIEN_PUBLIC_VLAN
args.label: CIEN public VLAN (only if Build CIEN)
args.description: Only when CIEN_PUBLIC is a facility port: its VLAN (auto = first free)

args.name: CIEN_PUBLIC_ADDR
args.label: CIEN public address (only if Build CIEN)
args.description: Only when CIEN_PUBLIC is a facility port: IPv4 CIDR

args.name: CIEN_PUBLIC_GW
args.label: CIEN public gateway (only if Build CIEN)
args.description: Blank = first usable address

args.name: CIEN_PUBLIC_ADDR6
args.label: CIEN public IPv6 (only if Build CIEN)
args.description: Only when CIEN_PUBLIC is a facility port: IPv6 CIDR

args.name: CIEN_PUBLIC_GW6
args.label: CIEN public IPv6 gateway (only if Build CIEN)
args.description: Blank = first usable address

args.name: CIEN_L2_IP
args.label: CIEN L2 address (only if Build CIEN)
args.description: CIEN DTN address on the Cape Town VLAN (Cape Town is 10.29.1.50)

args.name: CIEN_L2_FP
args.label: CIEN L2 facility port (only if Build CIEN)
args.description: Facility port for the CIEN data path

args.name: CIEN_L2_VLAN
args.label: CIEN L2 VLAN (only if Build CIEN)
args.description: VLAN on CIEN_L2_FP (auto = first free)

args.name: CIEN_PEER_IP
args.label: Cape Town IP (CIEN VLAN) (only if Build CIEN)
args.description: The Cape Town DTN's address on the CIEN data VLAN

args.name: CIEN_HOST
args.label: CIEN host (only if Build CIEN)
args.description: Pin the CIEN DTN VM to a worker, e.g. cien-w1.fabric-testbed.net (blank = FABRIC picks)

args.name: GLOBUS_USERS
args.label: Globus users
args.description: identity=account pairs, comma-separated, e.g. you@renci.org=komal. Only these identities can use the collections.

args.name: GLOBUS_CONTACT_EMAIL
args.label: Globus contact email
args.description: Contact shown on the endpoints

args.name: GLOBUS_ORG
args.label: Globus organization
args.description: Organization shown on the endpoints

args.name: GLOBUS_DISPLAY_NAME
args.label: Endpoint name
args.description: The site is appended: '... (FIU)'. Never rename a live endpoint - a new name makes a second collection.

args.name: GLOBUS_CLIENT_ID
args.label: Globus service client ID
args.description: Client UUID of a Globus Connect Server service credential (app.globus.org > Settings > Developers > your project > Add a service credential). With the secret, the weave writes it to the credential file (mode 0600) and later runs reuse it.

args.name: GLOBUS_CLIENT_SECRET
args.label: Globus service client secret
args.description: The secret shown once when the credential is created. Only needed on the first run (or to replace the credential); leave blank afterwards.

args.name: GLOBUS_CREDS_FILE
args.label: Globus credential file
args.description: Where the credential is kept. Blank = globus_creds.env in this weave. Fill it in by hand (see globus_creds.env.example) or let the two fields above write it.

args.name: GLOBUS_ADMIN
args.label: Globus administrator
args.description: Globus identity granted the administrator role on each endpoint (needs a Globus subscription; blank = none)

args.name: GLOBUS_PROJECT_ID
args.label: Globus Auth project
args.description: Globus Auth project (UUID) to create the endpoints in; the service credential must be an admin of it. Blank = Globus decides.

args.name: DATA_BASE
args.label: Collection directory
args.description: Directory on the DTN published as the mapped collection; each mapped user gets <dir>/<account>

args.name: CAPE_COLLECTION
args.label: Cape Town collection
args.description: Globus collection on the Cape Town DTN (SANReN GCP - Cape Town SC26)

args.name: DEMO_UI
args.label: Demo web UI
args.description: Install the demo web UI on each DTN (127.0.0.1 only; reach it with the SSH tunnel command the weave prints)

args.name: DEMO_UI_PORT
args.label: Demo UI port
args.description: Port of the demo web UI on the DTN and on your end of the tunnel

args.name: GLOBUS_NATIVE_CLIENT_ID
args.label: Globus native app client
args.description: Native-app client used to sign in from the demo UI / notebook (default: Globus SDK tutorial client; register your own for anything long-lived)

args.name: DATA_PATH
args.label: Globus data path
args.description: vlan = GCS advertises the Cape Town VLAN address for data (the demo); public = advertise the public uplink, so transfers with Cape Town work before the VLAN is mapped (also switchable live from the demo UI)

args.name: DATA_MTU
args.label: Data MTU
args.description: MTU on the data NIC; drops to 1500 automatically if jumbo frames do not reach Cape Town

args.name: DATA_NIC
args.label: Data NIC
args.description: NIC_Basic | NIC_ConnectX_5 | NIC_ConnectX_6 (FIU has ConnectX-5)

args.name: CORES
args.label: Cores
args.description: DTN VM cores

args.name: RAM
args.label: RAM (GB)
args.description: DTN VM memory (GCS needs 8+)

args.name: DISK
args.label: Disk (GB)
args.description: DTN VM disk; the collection lives on it

args.name: LEASE_DAYS
args.label: Lease (days)
args.description: Every slice is renewed to this many days

args.name: KEEP_SLICE
args.label: Keep slices
args.description: true = Stop / cleanup never delete anything. false = cleanup removes each Globus endpoint, then its DTN slice.

args.name: FORCE_DELETE
args.label: Force delete
args.description: Stop/cleanup: delete a DTN slice even if removing its Globus endpoint failed (remove it at app.globus.org first)
